chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū Ghurrah, who said:

I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever visits his brother for the sake of Allah, during illness or health, not coming to him for deception nor for reciprocal exchange, Allah will assign to him seventy thousand angels who will call out behind him:
You have done well, and Paradise is made better for you, for you are visitors of Allah, and you are a delegation of the Beneficent,
until he arrives at his house.'

So Yūsayr said to him: 'May I be sacrificed for you! And even if the place is distant?' He said: 'Yes, O Yūsayr, and even if the place is a year's journey, for Allah is Generous and the angels are numerous; they will escort him until he returns to his house.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting a brother in faith for the sake of Allah?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to establish ziyarat al-akhin as a profound act of worship that transcends physical proximity, with the Imam affirming that even a year's journey yields the same reward because Allah is Generous. The presence of seventy thousand angels serving as witnesses underscores the divine validation of this social bond, framing the visitor as the 'deputation of the Merciful' who maintains the spiritual network of the Ummah. This tradition is often cited by Shia jurists to emphasize that the intention of sincerity (ikhlas) and the absence of deceit are prerequisites for receiving this celestial honor.
